transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been having a harder time than usual since my district added this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on top of my regular teaching. I’m still managing to get through the day, but I feel pretty wound up and discouraged, and I’ve been putting off lesson plans and emails that I normally wouldn’t think twice about.
Have you noticed yourself losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or activities outside of work?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I still do things when I have time. It’s more that I’m tired or distracted, but I wouldn’t say I’ve completely lost interest.
Have you been feeling more worried or restless lately, like you can't relax even when you have some downtime?

Yes… more wound up, I’d say. Since this bilingual social-emotional learning rollout got added on top of my regular teaching, I can still do my job, but I don’t really feel settled, even when I’m off. I’m more discouraged than usual, and I catch myself putting off lesson plans and emails I’d normally just get done.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting, pacing, or feeling physically restless lately?

A little, maybe. I wouldn’t say I’m pacing around, but I do feel wound up in my body lately. Since that bilingual social-emotional learning rollout got added on top of my usual teaching, I’m still getting through the day… just not feeling like myself, and I keep putting off things like lesson plans and emails.
Outside of the stress related to work, have you noticed feeling down or losing pleasure in things most days, even when things aren’t particularly stressful?
Not really… I mean, I have off days, but I wouldn’t say I’m down or not enjoying things most days when work isn’t part of it. It feels more tied to the stressful stuff.
Have you noticed feeling down or having trouble enjoying things even during times when work isn’t on your mind?
I don’t think so. If work really isn’t on my mind, I can usually enjoy things okay… at least, I haven’t noticed that being a big problem.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things other than work, like everyday situations, your health, or other responsibilities?
Not especially. I mean, normal life stuff comes up, but I don’t think I’m worrying a lot about other things the way I am with work.
Do you find yourself feeling persistently worried or on edge about things other than this new teaching responsibility, even when those things aren’t particularly stressful or urgent?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I can get tense, but it’s usually around that teaching responsibility, not just everything in general.
Have you noticed any days where you just don't feel like enjoying anything, even things you usually like, even when work isn’t on your mind?
Not really… I can’t think of days like that. If work’s not weighing on me, I usually still want to do the things I like.
Have you had trouble controlling your worry, even when you know it might not be necessary, or has this stress affected other parts of your life, like relationships or sleep?

A little, yes. I’m still teaching and handling the main things, but… I’ve missed some planning deadlines, or pushed them back. And a couple colleagues have had to remind me about tasks I used to just get done on my own.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like trouble sleeping, muscle tension, or difficulty concentrating that aren’t directly related to the new teaching responsibilities?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really noticed anything like that outside of the teaching stuff. If I’m tense or distracted, it’s usually when I’m thinking about that.
When you’re completely away from work and not thinking about it at all, do you still find it hard to relax or feel restless?
No… I don’t think so. If I’m really away from it and not thinking about school, I can usually settle down okay.
When you're not thinking about work at all, do you ever feel sudden waves of anxiety or physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath that come out of nowhere?
No, I don’t think so. Not out of nowhere like that.
Have there been times lately where you didn’t feel like doing things you normally enjoy, even if just for a little while?
Not really… I mean, I have moments where I’m tired and don’t feel like doing much, but I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things I usually enjoy.
Have you felt down or discouraged even during times when work wasn't on your mind at all?

Not usually when it’s really off my mind. It’s more… since this district bilingual social-emotional learning rollout got added on top of my regular teaching, I’ve felt more wound up and discouraged than I normally would. I’m still managing, but it’s been harder, and I catch myself putting off lesson plans or emails I used to just do.
When you're not thinking about work at all, do you ever feel restless, anxious, or on edge for no clear reason?
I don’t think so. If I’m really not thinking about work, I don’t usually feel on edge for no reason.
Has this stress about the new teaching responsibilities made it harder for you to relax or function in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends, even when you're not at work?

A little, yes. I’m still doing my job and handling the basic things, but I’ve missed some planning deadlines, or pushed them back. And a couple colleagues have had to remind me about things I used to stay on top of pretty reliably.
Have you ever felt down, sad, or depressed for a day or more when work wasn’t on your mind at all?
I don’t think so. Not for a whole day if work really wasn’t on my mind.
